Customs

Recours Tarifaire

A formal process in which importers contest the customs duty rate or tariff classification assigned to goods by customs, invoking review procedures per WCO guidelines and national customs law, referenced in import declarations.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Recours Tarifaire?

In this glossary, Recours Tarifaire refers to: A formal process in which importers contest the customs duty rate or tariff classification assigned to goods by customs, invoking review procedures per WCO guidelines and national customs law, referenced in import declarations.

How is Recours Tarifaire used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Après que les douanes ont appliqué un taux de droit plus élevé, l’importateur a déposé un recours tarifaire en fournissant des fiches techniques pour étayer sa demande de reclassification."

Why does Recours Tarifaire matter in logistics?

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A formal process in which importers contest the customs duty rate or tariff classification assigned to goods by customs, invoking review procedures per WCO guidelines and national customs law, referenced in import declarations.

Operational example

After customs assigned a higher duty rate, the importer filed a tariff appeal providing technical data sheets to support their claim for reclassification.

Localized term

Recours Tarifaire

Localized example
